messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@finapps.com>, FinApps Procurement <procurement@finapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: FinApps — budget gap, savings levers & next steps

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for the call today — solid discussion. Quick recap and where we landed (so procurement has the numbers they asked for):

Pain points & goals
- Primary pain: per-interaction cost is eroding margin on your new invoice-parsing feature; current hosted LLM spend is unpredictable.
- Goal: move to a repeatable pilot that reduces per-call cost while keeping latency < 400ms for interactive flows and maintaining extraction accuracy.

What we heard (numbers from your side)
- Live usage: ~12k authenticated user interactions/day (weekdays) -> ~250k interactions/month.
- Avg tokens per interaction (prompt + user content + responses): ~1,800 tokens.
- Current estimated monthly LLM spend (3rd party): ~$42k/month (~$504k/year) — you noted a stretch annual budget of $150k for an MVP/first-year deployment.

Redwood quick TCO levers we discussed
- Continuous batching: grouping concurrent token requests; expected 1.6–2.2x effective token throughput improvement for your traffic shape.
- Prefix/KV caching: reusing repeated prompt prefixes (templates + common metadata) — 20–35% token reduction on requests that match templates.
- Model selection & quantization: switching to a cost-optimized variant with equivalent extraction quality reduces per-token unit cost by ~30% in our testbed.
- Routing & fallbacks: move non-sensitive traffic to lower-cost regions/variants with automatic fallback for failures.

Initial conservative TCO projection (pilot, 3 months)
- Baseline (no changes): ~42k/month.
- With batching + caching + model variant: estimated 35–55% reduction -> ~$19k–$27k/month (break-even vs baseline in ~2–6 months depending on integration effort).

Attachments: finapps_token_econ_model.xlsx (token-level model + assumptions), redwood_pilot_scope.pdf (pilot ops checklist and SLAs).

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Rishi / Redwood: provide a 1-page procurement-ready TCO summary and single-slide ROI (attached) — by Thu, 16 Sep.
2) Alex: confirm the 12k/day traffic figure or provide telemetry export (HubSpot or BigQuery sample) — by Fri, 17 Sep.
3) Marissa / Redwood: propose a technical kickoff agenda and minimal data contract (PII/PIA considerations) — by Mon, 20 Sep.
4) Procurement (FinApps): confirm target annual budget threshold (you mentioned $150k) and any approval gating — as soon as possible.

If these look right, I'll update the model with tighter unit costs and schedule a 30-min procurement Q&A next week.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi,

Appreciate the clear recap — this aligns with my notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Usage: the 12k/day is an average; peak weekdays see ~18k. We'll export a sample of the last 30 days (anonymized) for you — I'll drop that into the Drive link you shared.
- Budget: procurement's current baseline is $150k/year for new ML services. We could stretch to $220k with a 6–9 month documented ROI and exec sign-off.
- Risk items procurement flagged: data residency for invoices older than 7 years, and requirement for audit logs for token-level usage.

Can you make the one-pager explicitly call out: expected monthly cost range (with conservative and aggressive savings), security controls (KMS + audit logs), and estimated implementation effort (engineering weeks) so procurement can route this?

Happy to set a 30-min procurement sync next week. Dana Liu (procurement) is cc'd — Dana, can you propose 2 slots?

Thanks,
Alex
